 Korean media shocked by Big Bang's two nights at My Dinh Stadium.
 TPO - Big Bang's two concerts at My Dinh Stadium not only evoked memories for generations of fans but also sent a noteworthy signal to the Kpop industry. From the perspective of Korean media, Vietnam is gradually becoming a commercially attractive destination for international artists.
 Báo Tiền Phong • 26/10/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e Add Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e 0 On the nights of October 24th and 25th, Big Bang brought tens of thousands of fans to My Dinh Stadium in Hanoi as part of their XX: Cosmos world tour. For G-Dragon, Taeyang, and Daesung, this was a memorable milestone in the group's 20th anniversary.
 For the Vietnamese music market, the event has significance that goes beyond just a concert by Kpop stars.
 Surprises about Vietnam
 On October 26th, The Chosun Daily published an article titled "Big Bang's Vietnam Concert Shakes Kpop Market."
 Reporter An Jun Hyen noted that Big Bang's two concerts in Hanoi showed that Vietnam is emerging as an important market for the Kpop industry in Southeast Asia, thanks to its large fan base and growing purchasing power. 
 The success of Big Bang's two concerts has made the South Korean media look at Vietnam in a different light. Meanwhile, Financial News used data from 80,000 tickets for two nights of shows that sold out in about 10 minutes to analyze the shift in the market.
 According to the newspaper, Vietnam was once considered a difficult market to tap into for Kpop tours due to limited ticket purchasing power. However, economic growth and improved incomes are changing this perception .
 The newspaper quoted Yoon Hwi, CEO of Carpa, the concert co-organizer, as saying that rapid economic growth has significantly boosted ticket sales among Vietnamese audiences. According to him, the Vietnamese government's interest in the ripple effects of the culture and tourism industry has also opened up significant potential for the performing arts market.
 The Hankook Ilbo newspaper noted Big Bang's popularity in Hanoi, from tens of thousands of fans singing along to Korean songs to the increased demand for travel and accommodation.
 According to the newspaper, many fans have followed the group since their school days, and now, as adults, are willing to pay for large-scale musical experiences. This is a sign that Vietnam not only has a large fan base, but is also forming a customer group with sufficient purchasing power and loyalty to attract international tours.
 You may also like What does Vietnam have to offer to become a key market for Kpop?
 Big Bang's appeal in Hanoi is built on a foundation of a fan community that has been established for many years.
 The Chosun Daily noted the presence of fans over 30 years old, willing to pay for concert tickets and the trip to Hanoi. In addition, younger fans continue to discover Big Bang through Korean music and the members' influence in fashion and popular culture.
 The combination of a mature, affluent audience and a new generation of listeners provides the foundation for long-term market growth. 
 Big Bang has a large and strong fan base in Vietnam. Another factor making Vietnam attractive is its potential to transform music events into broader economic activity. Prior to the concert, The Korea Times reported that hotel searches in Hanoi on Klook in July increased by approximately 50% among Vietnamese users and 30% among international travelers compared to the same period last year. Searches for trips to Hanoi in October on Traveloka more than quadrupled.
 Following the event, The Chosun Daily cited a forecast from the Hanoi Tourism Association that the number of visitors during the concert could reach 175,000-190,000, with tourism revenue reaching 800 billion VND.
 These are projected figures for tourism activity during the relevant period, not confirmed revenue from the two nights of performances alone. Nevertheless, data on accommodation, travel, and spending suggests the concert has the potential to create a ripple effect that extends beyond the stadium.
 Big Bang's inclusion of Hanoi in their world tour alongside Tokyo, London, Paris, Singapore, and Sydney has also attracted attention. According to The Chosun Daily , this is the group's first concert in Vietnam, although Big Bang previously performed at a music event in 2012.
 Previous events show that Vietnam is no longer an unfamiliar market for international organizers. BlackPink attracted around 67,000 fans in Hanoi in 2023, while G-Dragon had approximately 100,000 fans during his two-day performance in Hung Yen in 2025.
 You may also like This series of activities helps to strengthen the organizers' confidence in their ability to attract audiences and boost domestic purchasing power. 
 Vietnam is on track to become a key market for Kpop music exports. However, two successful concerts do not necessarily mean Vietnam will become a regular destination for all major artists. Maintaining its appeal depends on organizational costs, infrastructure quality, licensing procedures, event safety, operational capacity, and actual commercial success.
 The success of a band with a long-standing fanbase cannot be applied directly to every artist.
 The takeaway from Big Bang's two nights in Hanoi is a shift in how the Vietnamese market is perceived. When audiences can fill stadiums, sing along to Korean songs, and create a buzz on international social media, Vietnam shows that it not only has a large fan base but also possesses significant commercial potential.
